title: This is the AMD Helios HPE Juniper QFX5252 Switch Tray at OCP 2026
gist: ServeTheHome's OCP 2026 look at HPE Juniper's QFX5252 switch tray for AMD's Helios rack: two Broadcom Tomahawk 6 chips, liquid cooling, retimers and heavy copper, which the author uses to argue for co-packaged optics.

insights.claim: The HPE Juniper QFX5252 tray for AMD's Helios rack is a double-wide, 1OU liquid-cooled tray with two Broadcom Tomahawk 6 102.6T switch chips, built to scale up within the rack rather than out through front-panel connectors.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Shows AMD's rack-scale scale-up fabric is built on Broadcom merchant switch silicon, a Broadcom beneficiary.
insights.locator: This is the AMD Helios HPE Juniper QFX5252 Switch Tray

insights.claim: Helios uses Tomahawk 6 rather than Tomahawk Ultra because Ultra is a 112G PAM4 SerDes part (512 lanes) while Helios uses 224G PAM4 SerDes.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: SerDes speed, not switch category, decides which Broadcom chip lands in scale-up designs.
insights.locator: There are two switch chips inside

insights.claim: The tray's cable connectors sit far from the switch chips with liquid-cooled retimers in between, and the author notes AMD is big on retimers while NVIDIA has worked to remove them.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Retimer content favors vendors like those supplying retimers in AMD systems and marks a design divergence from NVIDIA.
insights.quote: AMD is big on retimers while NVIDIA has worked to remove them
insights.locator: You will notice that the cabled connections

insights.claim: Helios still uses fans and air cooling for some components in the tray, unlike NVIDIA's push to move fans out of the AI rack.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: AMD's rack is less fully liquid-cooled than NVIDIA's direction, affecting thermal-vendor content.
insights.locator: You can see the fans and airflow guides

insights.claim: The author argues the tray's retimers plus an enormous array of copper cables illustrate why the industry will eventually go to co-packaged optics, which would simplify the design.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Rack-scale copper complexity and insertion force are cited as drivers for CPO adoption.
insights.locator: When we say copper inside a rack

insights.claim: Because of the dense blind-mate back panel, insertion force for the tray into the Helios rack is significant, requiring very long latches.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Mechanical constraints of dense copper backplanes are a practical scaling limit.
insights.locator: You can see the HPE QFX5252 label
